findings.explanation: del_ts exists only inside the Machine arm and is not a field of the final result set. mac_stuck >= 1 alone is not a page condition in the SPL, which also requires mac_del_age >= 45. The SPL tiers (page, warn, info) and the warn conditions are never described, so the prose threshold does not match the detection.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the real severity logic: page when ControlPlaneMachineSet unavailable counters are 1 or more, when a Machine has been Deleting for 45 minutes or more, or when MachineHealthCheck drift exists and remediationsAllowed is 0. Warn on storm-level phase churn, MachineSet gaps of 2 or more, or any MachineHealthCheck drift.

findings.explanation: detailedImplementation (Case 6), the title and the value text promise capacity-watermark risk detection. The SPL only displays max_nodes_hint, region_hint and escalation_tier. No severity or recommended_action branch compares node or Machine counts to max_nodes_hint, so no watermark logic exists.
findings.quote: warn severity combines positive ms_gap with lookup max_nodes_hint suggesting proximity to ceiling
findings.suggested_fix: Either state that max_nodes_hint is display-only context for responders, or ask the SPL owners to add a real comparison of total Machine count to max_nodes_hint. The text must match whichever is implemented.

findings.explanation: ControlPlaneMachineSet status is documented with replicas, readyReplicas, updatedReplicas and unavailableReplicas. status.unavailableMachines looks invented. MachineSet status normally has replicas, fullyLabeledReplicas, readyReplicas and availableReplicas, with no unavailableReplicas, which is a Deployment field. The SPL's cpms_u, cpms_ur and ms_unavail inputs may therefore never populate.
findings.quote: map status.unavailableMachines and status.unavailableReplicas when your OpenShift minor exposes them
findings.suggested_fix: Check the ControlPlaneMachineSet and MachineSet CRD schemas on a live OpenShift 4.14+ cluster (oc explain controlplanemachineset.status and oc explain machineset.status). Use only fields that exist, for example derive MachineSet unavailable as spec.replicas minus status.availableReplicas.

findings.explanation: The OpenShift Machine API (machine.openshift.io, machine-api-operator) carries provider configuration in Machine spec.providerSpec and status.providerStatus. AWSMachine and similar kinds, with infrastructureRef and the x-k8s.io finalizers and taints, belong to upstream Cluster API (CAPI) and are not the standard objects on the production MAPI path. The text appears to mix the two.
findings.quote: including provider-specific infrastructure references such as AWSMachine, AzureMachine, GCPMachine, or VSphereMachine objects that ultimately bind provider IDs to Kubernetes Node identities
findings.suggested_fix: Verify with oc get machine -o yaml on an IPI cluster. Refer to providerSpec and providerStatus for MAPI, and move any CAPI object names (AWSMachine and so on) into a clearly labelled Cluster API tech-preview note. Check the real finalizer names, since Machine API Machines use machine.machine.openshift.io rather than machine.cluster.x-k8s.io.

findings.explanation: The grounding guide lists Splunk Connect for Kubernetes (3743) and the Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Kubernetes, not a Splunk Add-on for Kubernetes named Splunk_TA_kubernetes. The OTel receiver is called k8sobjects (k8sObjects in the Helm values), not kubernetesObjects. dataSources also says a Universal Forwarder is Splunkbase 617, but the UF is not a Splunkbase app and has no such modular input. The deterministic check already flags 617 as unknown to the cached catalog.
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for Kubernetes (`Splunk_TA_kubernetes`) or OpenTelemetry Collector with kubernetesObjects receiver
findings.suggested_fix: Look up the actual add-on and collector names. Use the Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Kubernetes with the k8sobjects receiver and k8s_events, as the container-platforms guide shows. Remove the UF-as-Splunkbase-617 claim unless a real Splunkbase app is identified.

findings.explanation: The data is custom JSON snapshots of machine.openshift.io objects (sourcetypes openshift:machine and others). No add-on in the grounding maps these to the CIM Application_State (ports, processes, services) or Inventory (endpoint hardware and software inventory) models. The SPL does not use CIM, so the mapping looks aspirational.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm that field aliases and tags actually populate these datamodels for these sourcetypes. If not, set cimModels to an empty list and drop the dataModelAcceleration paragraph.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified with a generic team reviewer handle and a bulk lastReviewed date. There is no SME sign-off evidence, and the field names above are doubtful.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to a non-verified value such as draft or community until a named SME confirms the Machine API fields, sourcetypes and SPL on a live cluster.

findings.explanation: This is the generator's self-check text and leaked into reader-facing content. It also has no value for someone implementing the detection. The same applies to the 'Fenced SPL must match the spl JSON field exactly' line in Step 3.
findings.quote: Closing checklist: five em-dash step headers are present; Step 3 fenced SPL matches the spl field exactly; multisearch lists four API snapshot arms;
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the authoring checklist and the 'must match the spl JSON field exactly' sentence.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The SPL runs stats, sort and streamstats inside the multisearch subsearches. multisearch accepts only streaming commands, so the search should fail with a non-streaming command error. See https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/SearchReference/Multisearch. The arms need to be rebuilt with append or a single base search, or the aggregation moved outside multisearch.

phase_tick counts Running as well as Deleting and Provisioning, then sums per cluster over a 6-hour window. With snapshots every 3 to 5 minutes, any cluster with a few Machines far exceeds mac_phase_evt >= 10, and any Machine with 4 consecutive snapshots hits mac_phase_burst >= 4. The warn tier would fire permanently. Remediation storms need phase transitions, not Running counts.

The title promises Capacity Watermark Risks. The SPL does not compare Machine or node counts to max_nodes_hint, and it implements only the MachineHealthCheck, Machine, MachineSet and ControlPlaneMachineSet signals. 'Cluster API' also conflicts with the Machine API objects actually queried.

The tstats query uses nodename=Inventory and nodename=Application_State, with Inventory.dest and Application_State.dest and no dataset names. CIM datamodel root datasets are normally All_Inventory and All_Application_State, so the nodename and field prefixes need verifying. Inventory.vendor_product also needs checking. The query would not return OpenShift Machine API data without custom mappings.

summary: The long-form implementation text is detailed, but the description and test text are word salad built from SPL fragments and do not match the SPL's severity logic. Several Machine API status fields look invented, the capacity-watermark promise is not implemented in the SPL, and the SPL itself uses non-streaming commands inside multisearch.
